newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Feb 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Feb 12.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- WEN WEI PO -- Veteran Singapore political leader Lee Kuan Yew said he was confident towards the future of Hong Kong and that Hong Kong people could continue to enjoy prosperity if they did not interfere with Chinese politics.

-- University students in Beijing were concerned about the Hong Kong handover. They had set up electronic countdown displays in campuses, held seminars and organised cycle rallies from Beijing to Shenzhen promoting the historical significance of Hong Kong's return to China.

-- TA KUNG PAO -- About 3,600 couples in Shanghai got divorced last year. In 80 percent of the cases, the wives took the initiative to leave their husbands. Many Chinese men could not put up with the fact that their wives earned more or occupied a higher position.
-- SING TAO -- Hongkong Electric had rejected China Light & Power's offer to supply it with electricity, saying the suggestion was "neither viable nor justifiable".

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Investment house ING Barings said that Hong Kong banks had the highest standards of disclosure in Asia. A study also found Hong Kong among the worst politicies in the region.
-- Shum Yip Investment was set to receive a boost through asset injection, after it was floated as the flagship arm of the Shenzhen municipal government.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- China was believed to have sent a positive signal to the local pro-China camp that the shelved Central Provident Fund would be re-examined by the Special Administrative Region government.

-- National Mutual Holdings of Australia had targeted China as a key market as it fleshed out its role as the Asian arm of one of the industry's global heavyweights. It planned to double its representation in China this year by opening three more local offices.
